chosen_bullets: If people rely on your income for this EMI, you need death cover for at least the outstanding loan. Loan cover pays the bank directly; a term plan pays your family, who can clear the loan or use the money elsewhere.

choices.chosen_text: If clearing the loan is the only goal, reducing cover (tracks your outstanding balance) is usually enough — you are not paying for cover on money you have already repaid. Level cover costs more; choose it only if your family needs more than what is still owed on the loan.

chosen_bullets: If clearing the loan is the only goal, reducing cover (tracks your outstanding balance) is usually enough — you are not paying for cover on money you have already repaid.

choices.chosen_text: If you buy loan cover, paying the premium outside the loan keeps interest off that amount — when the bank allows it. If they add it to your principal, you repay it with interest for the full loan term.
chosen_bullets: If you buy loan cover, paying the premium outside the loan keeps interest off that amount — when the bank allows it. If they add it to your principal, you repay it with interest for the full loan term.

choices.chosen_text: If your family would need cash after the loan is cleared, loan cover may not be the right product — the payout goes to the bank first on your Certificate of Insurance, and the nominee only gets what is left if the certificate allows it.

chosen_bullets: If your family would need cash after the loan is cleared, loan cover may not be the right product — the payout goes to the bank first on your Certificate of Insurance, and the nominee only gets what is left if the certificate allows it.

choices.chosen_text: If you can get a term plan for the full loan amount, compare that first — the nominee gets paid, the cover can outlast the loan, and it usually stays if you prepay or switch. Loan cover (bank paid first, often reducing cover) is mainly worth it when age or health makes term hard to get.
